newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Abbott plans to invest $30 in Irish operations.
newsitem.headline: Abbott plans to invest $30 in Irish operations.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories plans to invest $30 million in expanding its operations in Ireland, the minister for Enterprise and Employment Richard Bruton said on Monday.

The investment, with the support of both Forbairt and the IDA, will create an additional 75 jobs in Ireland, and bring Abbott's total new investment over the last three years to $50 million, the minister said.
Bruton welcomed the plans as 'a vote of confidence... by a huge global multi-national'.

Abbott, headquartered in Chicago, is a leading manufacturer of pharmaceuticals, nutritional products, hospital products and diagnostics. In 1996 it reported sales of $11 billion worldwide, with an annual expenditure in Ireland of 60 million Irish punts. The company set up in Sligo in 1972.
